memos.risk:
Risk call on PEAQ: I'd refuse this one, not size it.

The brief fits the operator profile, and the numbers look worse than break-even. Bundle share is 1.0, top-3 share is 1.0, and the top-5 buyers took 99.8% of the first two minutes' buys (827 SOL from 18 buyers). Last 15 minutes: 9.89 SOL bought against 9.29 sold, sell-to-buy near 0.94, net flow only 0.6 SOL, and the price is flat (+0.11%) after a 116x run. That is distribution pressure hidden under a flat tape, and the 0.13% drawdown from the 30-minute high says nothing about whether supply is still being unloaded.

Pool depth of 920 SOL is deep enough that a $20 ticket would not be impacted much, so the fees (1.4-5.1%) are not the binding problem. The problem is exit liquidity: concentrated holders selling into a thin retail bid.

Refuse at any size. If the desk wants to revisit, the trigger would be the operator's share of supply falling materially with sell-to-buy staying well below 0.5 across several windows.
memos.scout:
Honest case for buying PEAQ now: thin. The brief shows real, recent two-sided activity: 43 buyers and 30 sellers in the last 15 minutes, $2.3k volume, and a net flow of +0.6 SOL, so the book isn't dead. The price is holding within 0.13% of its 30-minute high after a 116x run, with a deep 920 SOL pool that should absorb a $20 ticket with modest impact.

But the rest argues against it. This is an operator-class launch: 827 SOL bought in the first two minutes by 18 wallets, with the top 5 buyers holding 99.8% and bundled supply at 100%. Recent flow is roughly even (9.9 SOL bought vs 9.3 sold), which looks more like supply changing hands than new demand arriving. The flat tape at the top of a pumped curve is what distribution looks like from the outside, and operator-backed coins have been about break-even at best, before our 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost.

Scout verdict: no case strong enough to buy. Recommend skipping.
memos.skeptic: Most likely loss: insider distribution by the operator. Top-3 holders own 100% of the curve (bundle_share 1.0, top3_share 1.0), and 827 SOL came from 18 buyers in the first two minutes after graduation, with the top 5 buyers taking 99.8% of that. That is a concentrated operator position, not organic demand. The last 15 minutes show 9.89 SOL bought against 9.29 SOL sold across 30 sellers, a net flow of only 0.6 SOL, so the price is flat (+0.11%) while the operator is already exiting into thin volume. The 116x return over 30 minutes is a sign the operator's cost basis is far below current price, which gives them every reason to sell. A 1-2% move cannot cover the 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost, and the 0.13% drawdown from the 30-minute high says the price has not yet begun to fall in earnest. Expected outcome is a loss after fees. Skip.
